spec.scope: Fix pass, exactly four items, nothing else. No git commit/push/stash/reset/checkout--; edit local files only. 1. Unsubscribe/subscribe race between SubscriptionManager (browser last-unsubscribe) and Services.watch_symbol (rule path). 2. Drain queued alerts on shutdown, bounded by a short timeout. 3. Backoff after a failed alert batch write. 4. INFO logging for the `app` loggers so "rule fired: ..." is visible under uvicorn/docker.
spec.design_race_fix: Chosen approach: one asyncio.Lock owned by Services (e.g. self._upstream_lock) that serializes every upstream subscribe/unsubscribe decision-plus-call. It is taken inside Services._up_subscribe, Services._up_unsubscribe (the callbacks handed to SubscriptionManager) and around the upstream call in Services.watch_symbol. Inside the lock each path re-reads current state at the moment it acts: - _up_unsubscribe: skip if symbol in self.watchlist (already the case) or ref_count(symbol) > 0; else await upstream.unsubscribe. - watch_symbol: add to self.watchlist first (synchronously, before waiting for the lock, so a queued unsubscribe decision made later sees it), then under the lock skip if ref_count(symbol) > 0, else await upstream.subscribe (failure still logged by type only, request still succeeds). - _up_subscribe: unchanged logic (skip if watched), now under the lock. Why this one: the race is that two independent awaits to the upstream can complete in the wrong order. A single lock makes the upstream calls totally ordered, so the last call always reflects the latest state; the watchlist add being synchronous means any unsubscribe that starts after it is skipped, and any unsubscribe already in flight finishes before watch_symbol's subscribe is sent. The alternative (re-check watchlist after the unsubscribe await and resubscribe) leaves a window where the symbol is briefly unsubscribed and can double-subscribe; the lock avoids both. Deadlock check: SubscriptionManager holds its own _lock while calling the callbacks (which take the Services lock); watch_symbol takes only the Services lock and reads ref_count without taking the manager lock. Lock order is always manager lock -> Services lock, so no cycle. The Services lock must never be held across a manager method call. Invariant kept: no duplicate subscribe for an already-subscribed symbol; on_tick untouched.
spec.files_to_touch: backend/app/main.py (lock, _up_subscribe/_up_unsubscribe/watch_symbol; logging setup in create_app or module level; optionally shutdown ordering) backend/app/db.py (Database.close drain; Database._alert_writer backoff) backend/tests/test_watchlist_alerts.py (new tests for items 1-4; or a small new test file only if the existing one gets unwieldy) backend/tests/fakes/fake_db.py only if a fake needs a drain/close hook; subscription_manager.py, routers/rules.py, config.py, .env.example are expected NOT to change.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A watched symbol never ends up unsubscribed upstream when a browser's last unsubscribe is in flight while a rule is created. Test (deterministic, Services level, in the style of the existing BlockingUpstream tests, async, no timing sleeps): define UnsubBlockingUpstream(FakeFinnhubClient) whose unsubscribe records "unsub-start", sets an `entered` Event, awaits a `release` Event, then applies the effect; subscribe applies its effect immediately. Effects are appended to one ordered list and a `state` set (add on subscribe, discard on unsubscribe). Steps: s=_services(); s.upstream=UnsubBlockingUpstream(); await s.subscriptions.subscribe("c1","AAPL"); t1=create_task(s.subscriptions.disconnect("c1")); await entered.wait(); t2=create_task(s.watch_symbol("AAPL")); yield to the loop a fixed small number of times (await asyncio.sleep(0) x N, no wall-clock wait); release.set(); await gather(t1,t2). Assert: "AAPL" in s.watchlist and the final upstream state contains "AAPL" (last effective op for AAPL is a subscribe); no subscribe was issued while "AAPL" was already in the upstream state. MUST FAIL on iteration-2-baseline code (there watch_symbol subscribes immediately and the unsubscribe lands last, final state empty) and PASS after the fix. Verify by running the new test against the baseline main.py (e.g. a temp copy outside the repo tree or by reading the baseline diff); do not discard working-tree changes to do so.

The reverse orderings and existing coordination tests still pass and stay deterministic: browser subscribe in flight then rule (one subscribe total); rule in flight then browser (one subscribe total); browser leaves a watched symbol (no unsubscribe); rule created while a browser holds the symbol (no subscribe). Add one test: two concurrent watch_symbol calls for the same new symbol produce exactly one upstream subscribe. No deadlock: all new tests wrap awaits in asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=5) so a deadlock fails rather than hangs.

On Database.close(), alerts already in the alert queue are written before the alert writer is cancelled and the pool is closed, bounded by a short timeout (a few seconds, module-level constant so tests can shrink it). Test with a stub pool (fake object with acquire() async-CM and executemany recording rows) assigned to a Database instance with a running writer: enqueue N alerts, call close(), assert all N rows reached executemany before the pool close was called. Never hangs: second test makes the stub executemany block forever (or raise on every call) with the timeout patched to ~0.1s; close() must return within a bounded time (wrapped in wait_for) and still close the pool. close() with an empty queue, with no pool, and called twice must not raise.

After an alert batch write fails (batch plus row-by-row retry), the writer sleeps briefly (default about 1s, capped, module constant so it can be patched) before the next batch attempt; a persistently failing pool therefore yields at most about one failure-log burst per backoff interval, not a hot loop. Test: patch the backoff to a small value (e.g. 0.05s) and record calls via a patched asyncio.sleep or a stub whose executemany/execute always raise; enqueue alerts, assert the sleep hook was invoked after the failure and that the number of executemany attempts over a fixed number of event-loop yields is bounded (not growing unboundedly). A successful write does not sleep. Test also asserts enqueue_alert / Services.on_tick remain non-blocking (put_nowait only; on_tick returns without awaiting the backoff), e.g. enqueue_alert called while the writer is sleeping returns immediately and the item is later written once the pool recovers. The backoff sleep must remain cancellable so close() is not delayed by it beyond the drain timeout.

After create_app() (or import of app.main), logging.getLogger("app") has effective level INFO and an INFO record emitted from app.main (the "rule fired: ..." line) is emitted to a handler when no root handler is configured, i.e. visible under `uvicorn app.main:app`. Test: in a fresh state, assert getLogger("app").getEffectiveLevel() <= INFO and that a "rule fired" INFO record appears in caplog when a tick crosses a rule threshold (reuse the existing alert-enqueue test pattern). Handler installation must be idempotent (calling create_app twice does not add duplicate handlers; assert handler count unchanged) and must not touch the "uvicorn", "uvicorn.error" or "uvicorn.access" loggers or the root logger level. No new dependency; no new setting.

`pytest` from backend/ passes offline (no network, no Postgres); with TEST_DATABASE_URL pointing at an empty test DB the real-Postgres tests (test_rules_postgres.py and any alert tests there) still pass. Existing tests are not weakened or deleted. Frontend untouched, so `npm test` is unaffected.

assumptions.a: "Short timeout" for the drain is 3 to 5 seconds; backoff is 1s fixed (or doubling capped at a few seconds); exact values are the implementer's call but must be patchable constants.
Only alerts are drained; the tick queue is best-effort and may still be cancelled immediately (not in the four items).
Backoff applies to the alert writer only, not the tick worker (out of scope).
Logging handler goes on the "app" logger (propagate left as-is) only when neither it nor root has handlers, so it does not double-print under pytest or a configured root.
Services.shutdown ordering (upstream.stop, then db.close) is already correct for draining since stopping upstream ends new ticks; no change required.

edge_cases.e: Upstream subscribe/unsubscribe raising inside the lock must release the lock (use async with) and not wedge later calls.
Unsubscribe in flight, rule created, then a browser re-subscribes: no upstream traffic beyond the rule's single subscribe.
Upstream is None: lock paths are no-ops, rule creation still returns 201.
Shutdown while the writer is mid-backoff or mid-batch: drain bounded, then cancel; no unhandled task exception.
Alerts enqueued while pool is down are not queued at all (enqueue_alert no-ops without a pool); drain must tolerate _pool None.
Alert queue refilling during drain: drain only needs to flush what was queued at close time and still honors the timeout.

risks.risk: Lock acquired in watch_symbol while the request handler waits behind a slow upstream unsubscribe delays the rule POST response; acceptable (bounded by upstream call), but upstream calls have no timeout today.
Lock-order mistake (holding Services lock while calling into SubscriptionManager) could deadlock; criterion 2 uses wait_for to surface it.
Drain via queue.join() requires task_done accounting in the writer; if the implementer instead polls empty(), a batch in flight may be lost. Test in criterion 3 checks rows written, not mechanism.
Logging config at import time can duplicate output if the host also configures root handlers; guarded by the idempotence/no-root-handler rule.

spec.dependencies: Existing only: asyncio, logging, pytest-asyncio (already used by the async tests), tests/fakes/fake_finnhub.py FakeFinnhubClient, FakeDatabase. Baseline snapshot at .claude/team/T008/iteration-2-baseline/ (read-only reference). No new packages.
spec.out_of_scope: Removing browser websockets or routers/symbols.py; /api/watchlist and /api/prices; latest_prices; fail-loud startup; tick-worker backoff or drain; upstream call timeouts; changing SubscriptionManager's public API or its own lock; frontend changes; new settings or env vars; reconfiguring uvicorn loggers; any git history or working-tree-discarding command.
spec.self_critique: Every item maps to criteria (1-2 race, 3 drain, 4 backoff, 5 logging, 6 suite). The race test is deterministic via Events and fixed loop yields, and fails on baseline because the unsubscribe completes after the immediate rule subscribe. Biggest remaining risk: the baseline-fail check depends on how the fake records effect order (must record at completion, not start), and the "N loop yields" must be enough for the baseline watch_symbol to run to its await; the implementer should confirm failure on baseline explicitly.
